findings.explanation: At line 98 the robot added the liquid from tube B6 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C2 in slot 3, the liquid from tube C6 in slot 3 and 2 more to wells C8, C10, C12, D8, D10, D12, H10 and H12 in slot 4, which already held the liquid from tube A6 in slot 3, the liquid from tube B1 in slot 3, the liquid from tube B2 in slot 3, the liquid from tube B6 in slot 3 and 4 more (this line did it 6 times). The addition was 14 to 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 110 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 5 while it still carried standard 1 (well A1 in slot 4), standard 2 (well A2 in slot 4), standard 3 (well A3 in slot 4), standard 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 2 more from an earlier step (this line did it 6 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 59 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, B2, B3 and 51 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 110, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 111 the tip touched the liquid in wells B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, C1 and 13 more in slot 4 while it still carried standard 1 (well A1 in slot 4), standard 2 (well A2 in slot 4), standard 3 (well A3 in slot 4), standard 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 4 more from an earlier step (this line did it 21 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. This is only a note, because one and the same line of the protocol sends this tip into all of these wells, which is what an author does with one reagent split over several wells. If they hold the same liquid, nothing is wrong. If they hold different samples, it is a mix-up. The protocol does not declare its liquids, so Provette cannot tell which.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 111, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
